question.problem:
Consider the following matrices:

$$
{B}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}],\,{B}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 0 & -3\end{aligned}],\,A=[\begin{aligned}-2 & -6 \\ 0 & 12\end{aligned}]
$$

If $B=\{{B}_{1},{B}_{2}\}$ is a basis of $\text{Span}\{{B}_{1},{B}_{2}\},$ and $[A]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],$ then ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=$
question.worked_solution:
We need to find ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ such that 

$$
{x}_{1}{B}_{1}+{x}_{2}{B}_{2}=A.
$$

Substituting the given information into the above equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 0 & -3\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & -6 \\ 0 & 12\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} & -2{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} \\ 0 & 3{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & -6 \\ 0 & 12\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding entries, we obtain

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=-2 \\ -2{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=-6 \\ 3{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2}=12.\end{aligned}
$$

 

The equations above give a linear system with the augmented matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -2 \\ -2 & 1 & -6 \\ 3 & -3 & 12\end{aligned}].
$$

Row-reducing the matrix using Gaussian elimination, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}M= & [\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -2 \\ -2 & 1 & -6 \\ 3 & -3 & 12\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-3){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\ ∼ & [\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -2 \\ 0 & 5 & -10 \\ 0 & -9 & 18\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=-2 \\ 5{x}_{2}=-10 \\ -9{x}_{2}=18.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second and third equations, we get ${x}_{2}=-2.$ From the first equation, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2(-2) & =-2 \\ {x}_{1} & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, $[A]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2\end{aligned}].$

Finally, ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=2+(-2)=0.$
